questions.stem: Point A has position vector (3, 7) and point B has position vector (−1, 2). Find the vector AB.
questions.explanation: AB = b − a = (−1 − 3, 2 − 7) = (−4, −5). A common error is computing a − b = (4, 5) instead, which gives BA.

questions.stem: The position vector of P is (5, −2) and PQ = (−3, 8). What is the position vector of Q?
questions.explanation: Position vector of Q = position vector of P + PQ = (5, −2) + (−3, 8) = (2, 6). The position vector gives coordinates relative to the origin.

questions.stem: Points A(2, 1), B(8, 5) and C(k, 3) are such that C is the midpoint of AB. What is the value of k?
questions.explanation: Midpoint of AB = ((2+8)/2, (1+5)/2) = (5, 3). So k = 5. Check: the y-coordinate 3 matches, confirming the midpoint calculation.

questions.stem: OA = (1, 4) and OB = (9, 0). Point P lies on AB such that AP:PB = 3:1. What is the position vector of P?
questions.explanation: AB = b − a = (8, −4). AP = 3/4 of AB = (6, −3). OP = OA + AP = (1, 4) + (6, −3) = (7, 1). Since AP:PB = 3:1, P is 3/4 of the way from A to B.

questions.stem: The distance between points with position vectors (2, −1) and (−2, t) is 5. Given t > 0, what is the value of t?
questions.explanation: Distance = sqrt((−2−2)² + (t−(−1))²) = sqrt(16 + (t+1)²) = 5. So 16 + (t+1)² = 25, giving (t+1)² = 9, t+1 = 3 (taking positive root since t > 0), t = 2.
